chunks: And ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: “Do not fumigate the shrouds, and do not apply perfume to your dead except with camphor, for indeed the deceased is in the position of the muḥrim.”

key_terms.الْأَكْفَانَ: the burial shrouds used for the deceased
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: a person in iḥrām, whose state entails restrictions including avoiding perfume
key_terms.بِالْكَافُورِ: with camphor, the permitted scented substance mentioned here
key_terms.مَوْتَاكُمْ: your dead, meaning the deceased persons being prepared for burial

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perfume a deceased person or their shroud in Islamic burial rites?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding funerary preparation, forbidding the perfuming of shrouds and the application of scent to the deceased except for camphor. It likens the deceased to a muḥrim, indicating a state in which ordinary perfume is to be avoided.
